_meta.indication: Treatment of adult patients with Cushing's disease for whom pituitary surgery is not an option or has not been curative

pivotal_trials.trial_name: Study B2305 (SOM230B2305), a Phase III pivotal trial in Cushing's disease
pivotal_trials.nct: Not stated in the FDA documents reviewed
pivotal_trials.design: Randomized, double-blind, 18-center, 6-month international trial comparing two uncontrolled pasireotide dose regimens (600 µg bid vs 900 µg bid)
pivotal_trials.population: Adult Cushing's disease patients with persistent/recurrent hypercortisolism despite prior pituitary surgery, or de novo patients who were poor surgical candidates; baseline 24-hour UFC >1.5 x ULN
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Proportion of responders at Month 6 (mean 24-hour UFC normalized to ≤ ULN without a dose increase during the period), assessed by individual dose group
pivotal_trials.n: 162 randomized patients dosed (82 in the 600 µg bid group, 80 in the 900 µg bid group)
pivotal_trials.result: UFC responders at Month 6: 15% (12/82) in the 600 µg bid group and 26% (21/80) in the 900 µg bid group. The 900 µg dose met the primary efficacy criterion (lower bound of two-sided 95% CI = 17%, exceeding the 15% non-inferiority margin); the 600 µg dose did not.

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (overall, N=162) were diarrhea (58%), nausea (52%), hyperglycemia (40%), cholelithiasis (30%), headache (28%), abdominal pain (24%), fatigue (19%), and diabetes mellitus (18%). Hyperglycemia/diabetes is a key risk; 5% of patients had ALT or AST >3x ULN; injection site reactions occurred in 17%.
target_moa: Cyclohexapeptide somatostatin analogue that binds and activates somatostatin receptors (notably hsst5, frequently over-expressed on corticotroph tumor cells), inhibiting ACTH secretion and thereby decreasing cortisol secretion

rems.type: No REMS was recommended; a Medication Guide (not part of a REMS) was submitted

advisory_committee.vote: Presented to the Endocrinologic and Metabolism Drugs Advisory Committee (EMDAC) on November 7, 2012; the committee rendered a unanimous vote of 'yes' to the question of whether the applicant had provided sufficient evidence for efficacy and safety to support marketing of pasireotide for the treatment of Cushing's disease

description.text: Fulfilled postmarketing requirement with Study CSOM230B2219 on managing Signifor-induced hyperglycemia and updated section 6 of labeling

citations.quote: This Prior Approval supplemental new drug application provides for the POSTMARKETING REQUIREMENT 1985-3: "A multi-center, randomized, clinical trial investigating the management of Signifor (pasireotide)-induced hyperglycemia in patients with Cushing's disease treated with Signifor", as stated in the approval letter dated December 14, 2012. The final report for Study CSOM230B2219 was included in this submission, and corresponding changes to section 6 of the package insert have been proposed.

orphan_indication.text: Orphan drug designation was granted in 2009 for this product for the Cushing's disease indication

citations.quote: The IND was submitted in 2006 and orphan drug designation was granted in 2009.
Because this drug product for this indication has an orphan drug designation, you are exempt from this requirement.

summary.text: Signifor was reviewed under Standard (not priority) review, received February 17, 2012, with orphan drug designation (granted 2009). It was presented to the EMDAC advisory committee on November 7, 2012 (unanimous 'yes' vote) and approved first cycle in 2012 for Cushing's disease, with three post-marketing requirements (registry, spontaneous-report analysis, and a hyperglycemia-management trial).
